results.text: Applying the vulnerability approach to the World Bank’s harmonized household surveys—estimating, for each economy, the probability that a household is living on less than the poverty line of the relevant income group over a few years, and identifying the consumption level at which this probability becomes low—yields economic security lines of about $6.00, $7.00, and $14.00 a day for the three income groups. This is roughly twice the corresponding poverty lines, but with wide variation across economies (Bolch et al. 2026). The threshold also shifts with the risks households face. In Europe and Central Asia, the income needed to maintain a low probability of falling into poverty rose by about 10 percent in real terms between 2008 and 2018 as the shocks pushing households into poverty grew larger (Bussolo et al. 2025). results.text: To investigate the disproportionate impact, two methods allow variation in the intensity of the shock faced by households (Kimura et al. 2026). In both cases, the average growth of the economy is maintained at the level indicated in Global Economic Prospects, June 2026 (World Bank 2026c), which captures the aggregate income and price shock. First, households are allocated sectoral growth rates based on their sector of employment. Second, inflation is allocated to households depending on their budget’s exposure to food and energy. Poorer households typically spend a greater share on food and energy and thus receive lower real income if the prices of these items rise. A distribution-neutral assumption, which is used as the baseline throughout the report, would instead assume the equal distribution of inflationary shocks.

Record maize harvests in South Africa (Crop Estimates Committee 2026) fixed fertilizer prices in some countries, such as India (PIB 2026), and the low take-up of fertilizers in Sub-Saharan Africa (FAO 2025) generally could mitigate the impact on food prices. answer: Chưa đủ bằng chứng trong kho để trả lời. Đã dùng hết lượt tìm kiếm. Đoạn duy nhất được truy xuất nói về việc cú sốc giá năng lượng tác động trực tiếp đến ngân sách hộ gia đình và gián tiếp qua chi phí vận tải lương thực, cùng với giá phân bón tăng. Tuy nhiên, đoạn này không nói về hộ nghèo, không so sánh mức độ nhạy cảm giữa hộ nghèo và hộ khác, và không giải thích tỷ trọng chi tiêu lương thực/năng lượng trong ngân sách hộ nghèo. Vì vậy không thể kết luận vì sao hộ nghèo nhạy cảm hơn.
